title: Ecosystem services in biologically diversified versus conventional farming systems: benefits, externalities, and trade-offs
methodology: Comparative review of diversified versus conventional farming systems.
limitations: Review of heterogeneous case studies; not a single experimental design.

chunks.text: Biologically diversified farming systems tend to support more biodiversity and associated ecosystem services than simplified conventional systems, including soil organic matter related functions and habitat for beneficial organisms. Trade-offs include management complexity and possible short-term yield or water costs. The review argues for evaluating multiple services together rather than optimizing one variable such as yield or irrigation.
